provenance.source: PR #6873 fix(headers): allow iterable objects to be a data source for the set method, squash-merged 2025-04-14 as 1b1f9ccdc
provenance.note: The PR widened the source branch from `utils.isHeaders` to any object with a Symbol.iterator and feeds each pair to the internal setter one at a time. Those calls pass the caller's rewrite flag, which is normally undefined, so for a name that already has a value the setter takes its overwrite branch: a repeated name keeps only the entry that came last. A native `Headers` carrying three `set-cookie` values therefore reaches the response/request path as one string instead of three. The later fix #6885 accumulates the pairs into a plain object, turning repeated keys into arrays, and hands that object to the bulk setter. Pre-existing: the collapse predates this PR — the isHeaders branch it replaces behaved the same way — so the reviewed hunk is the iterable source the fix rewrites, not the code that first lost the values.

keywords: each iteration overwrites the value stored before
duplicate values from a repeated key are dropped
only the last value of a repeated header survives
repeated values are overwritten instead of accumulated
repeated pairs lose every value but the last
bugs.note: one internal setter call per pair, with no accumulation, so a repeated name overwrites its earlier values instead of building the array a native Headers hands over; the fix gathers the pairs first and lets the bulk setter merge duplicates
